# Model side-by-side, slice 3 (the contract draft)

## Result (2026-10-23, BUILD-3; decision 36)

**Opus 5.5 drafts the contract.** An independent close reading of both drafts below (prompt `draft.v1`), done as a
New York real estate lawyer would, found Opus decisively better [INFERENCE: one reviewer, one deal]:

- **Opus** follows the long form's mechanics and cites the right law: risk of loss under GOL §5-1311; TP-584 and
  RP-5217 named, and no mansion tax below $1 million; a bargain-and-sale deed with covenant and the Lien Law §13
  trust-fund covenant; the escrow terms (a 10-business-day objection window, IOLA, payment into court); the
  buyer protected if a commitment is withdrawn through no fault of theirs; a search for certificates of occupancy
  and open permits; an ELAP-certified lab for the well and a NY-licensed home inspector; the detector affidavit
  under Executive Law §378; and the e-signature law, with the deed kept in ink.
- **Sonnet** reads more simply, but has errors a lawyer would flag on first reading. Rider R1 says the buyer "must
  close even if the lender later refuses to fund", which puts the $62,900 deposit at risk. The closing date is
  "fixed" with no adjournment. Clause 14 says the deed must state the price. It has no escrow objection procedure
  and no search for certificates of occupancy.
- **Both v1 drafts** leaked the software's vocabulary into the contract ("intake screen", "CP-04"). Opus also
  invented numbers the deal did not give: a $2,500 cure cap, a 5 gpm well-flow pass mark, a one-year survival
  period. Both came from how the context and prompt were worded, not from the model.

**Prompt `draft.v2`** fixes the shared problems:

- the disclosures are given in the contract's own terms, with no screen or record codes;
- the software stays out of the contract;
- where the deal gives no number, the draft leaves a blank (`[$______]`, `[__] days`) and the notes to the parties
  say so;
- facts given for information are not representations.

The recorded Opus `draft.v2` run (12,841 output tokens, $0.273, 119 s) passed every code check. It has none of the
software's words, 28 blanks for the parties, and a rider clause R8, "Information given, not representations". It
keeps the strengths above.

**Cost:** Opus is about $0.27 to $0.30 a draft, against $0.18 for Sonnet. That is about $0.10 more a live run, as
the spec foresaw, and nothing in replay. Latency is about 2 to 3 minutes either way, so the hosted demo replays
the recorded draft. Opus is used nowhere else.

**Residential Contract of Sale and Rider: One-Family House, 146 Route 292, Holmes, Town of Pawling, Dutchess County, New York (Demonstration Draft)**

- **1. Premises.** [SELLER_1] agrees to sell and [BUYER_1] agrees to buy the one-family house and land at 146 Route 292, Holmes, Town of Pawling, Dutchess County, New York (about 4.18 acres according to the public record), together with the buildings on it and everything permanently attached to them. That includes the heating system and oil tank, the well and well pump and equipment, the septic system, plumbing and electrical systems, light fixtures, and any storm windows, screens and doors. It also includes [SELLER_1]'s rights, if any, in the road in front of the land and in any adjoining strips. The legal description in [SELLER_1]'s own deed will be used in the new deed. Together these are called the Premises.
- **2. Personal Property.** No items of personal property (things not attached to the house) are included in this sale beyond what clause 1 describes. The accepted offer lists none. Rider clause R5 says how any item can be added. Anything of [SELLER_1]'s that is not included must be removed before closing.
- **3. Purchase Price.** The purchase price is $629,000. It is payable as follows: (a) $62,900 (10% of the price) as the deposit under clause 6, paid when the contract is signed; and (b) the balance of $566,100 at closing, by the acceptable funds described in clause 7. The balance includes the proceeds of [BUYER_1]'s mortgage loan under clause 8 and Rider clause R1.
- **4. Existing Mortgage.** [BUYER_1] is not taking over any mortgage now on the Premises. [SELLER_1] will pay off and have discharged, at or before closing, every existing mortgage and similar lien on the Premises. The payoff may come from the purchase price as clause 20 allows. [SELLER_1] will ask each lender for a written payoff statement before closing.
- **5. Purchase Money Mortgage.** Not applicable. [SELLER_1] is not lending any part of the price to [BUYER_1]. [BUYER_1]'s financing comes from a third-party lender under clause 8 and Rider clause R1.
- **6. Downpayment in Escrow.** [BUYER_1] will deliver the $62,900 deposit to the escrow holder named in Rider clause R9 when both parties have signed this contract. The escrow holder will keep the deposit in a separate escrow account, will not mix it with its own money, and will release it only (a) at closing to [SELLER_1], as part of the price; (b) to [BUYER_1], if [BUYER_1] cancels in time under a contingency in this contract or this contract is properly ended for a reason that entitles [BUYER_1] to the deposit; (c) to [SELLER_1], if this contract is properly ended for [BUYER_1]'s default; or (d) as both parties agree in writing or as a court orders. If the parties disagree about the deposit, the escrow holder may keep it until they agree or a court decides, or may pay it into court. The escrow holder is a stakeholder, not a party to the sale, and is not liable for acting in good faith.
- **7. Acceptable Funds.** The deposit may be paid by wire transfer or by a check that clears and is collected before it is released. All money due at closing must be paid by wire transfer of immediately available funds, by an official bank check or certified check drawn on a bank in New York State, or by a check from the title company's or an attorney's escrow account. A personal check is not acceptable at closing. Checks are payable as the receiving party directs.
- **8. Mortgage Commitment Contingency.** [BUYER_1]'s obligation to buy depends on [BUYER_1] getting a written mortgage commitment within 30 days after the contract date (the Commitment Date). The commitment is for a conventional loan on the Premises, as set out in Rider clause R1. If [BUYER_1] does not get a commitment, [BUYER_1] may cancel in the way Rider clause R1 describes and will get the full deposit back. [BUYER_1] must apply promptly and in good faith and must not do anything meant to cause the lender to refuse.
- **9. Permitted Exceptions.** [SELLER_1] will convey title subject only to these Permitted Exceptions: (a) zoning and building laws, so long as the Premises can still be used as a one-family house; (b) recorded easements for utilities and recorded covenants and restrictions that do not stop that use or reduce the Premises' value; (c) facts an accurate survey would show, so long as they do not interfere with that use and no building encroaches on another's land or on a road; (d) real estate taxes that are not yet due, which are adjusted at closing; and (e) anything [BUYER_1] accepts in writing. Mortgages, judgments, tax liens and other money liens are not Permitted Exceptions.
- **10. Governmental Violations and Orders.** [SELLER_1] will comply with every notice of violation or order against the Premises issued by a government agency before the contract date, and will pay for that work, if the notice is on record or [SELLER_1] knows of it. If [SELLER_1] does not finish the work before closing, [SELLER_1] may instead give [BUYER_1] a credit at closing for its reasonable cost, as the parties agree in writing. If the parties cannot agree on that, [BUYER_1] may cancel by written notice and get the full deposit back. Violations first noted after the contract date do not give [BUYER_1] the right to cancel, unless they are based on conditions that existed before the contract date and the cost to correct them is substantial.
- **11. Seller's Representations.** [SELLER_1] states that, to [SELLER_1]'s knowledge, as of the contract date and again at closing: (a) [SELLER_1] owns the Premises and has the right to sell them; (b) [SELLER_1] has not received notice of any pending condemnation, special assessment, lawsuit or governmental proceeding affecting the Premises that has not been disclosed in writing to [BUYER_1]; (c) [SELLER_1] is not a foreign person for federal tax purposes; and (d) the facts [SELLER_1] gave on the Property Condition Disclosure Statement delivered under Rider clause R6 are true, to the best of [SELLER_1]'s knowledge. The statement is not a warranty and is not a substitute for [BUYER_1]'s own inspections.
- **12. Condition of Property.** [BUYER_1] has been given the chance to inspect the Premises. Subject to the contingencies in Rider clauses R2, R3 and R4 and to the Property Condition Disclosure Statement, [BUYER_1] will take the Premises in their present condition, reasonable wear and tear excepted, and [SELLER_1] makes no other promise about their condition. Until closing, [SELLER_1] will maintain the Premises, lawn and grounds as they are today. At closing, [SELLER_1] will deliver the Premises vacant and broom-clean, with the heating, plumbing, electrical, well pump and septic systems in the working order they are in on the contract date. [SELLER_1] will remove all debris and all personal property not included in this sale. [BUYER_1] may walk through the Premises shortly before closing. Risk of loss by fire or other casualty stays with [SELLER_1] until closing. If the Premises are materially damaged before closing, [BUYER_1] may cancel and get the full deposit back, or may close and receive [SELLER_1]'s insurance proceeds or a credit.
- **13. Insurable Title.** [SELLER_1] must deliver title that a reputable title insurance company licensed in New York is willing to insure for [BUYER_1], at regular rates, free of everything except the Permitted Exceptions. If [BUYER_1] wants a lender's policy, the lender's title requirements must be met by [SELLER_1] only so far as they relate to the quality of [SELLER_1]'s own title.
- **14. Closing, Deed and Title.** At closing, [SELLER_1] will deliver to [BUYER_1] a bargain and sale deed with covenant against grantor's acts, in proper form for recording, signed in ink by [SELLER_1] and acknowledged before a notary public, as set out in Rider clause R8. The deed must state the true price and must convey the Premises free of everything except the Permitted Exceptions. The deed will be signed by every person who owns the Premises. [SELLER_1] will also deliver any other documents this contract requires, including the transfer tax forms.
- **15. Closing Date and Place.** The closing will take place on December 22, 2026, which is 60 days after the contract date as the parties have agreed. It will be held at a place the parties agree on in writing or, if they have not, at the office of the title company or of the lender's attorney in or near Dutchess County. The parties may agree in writing to move the date. If either party cannot close on that date, the other may give written notice setting a new reasonable date and making time of the essence for that date. Closing may be completed without both parties present if the title company has the signed papers and the funds.
- **16. Conditions to Closing.** [BUYER_1] is not required to close unless: (a) [SELLER_1]'s statements in clause 11 are still true; (b) [SELLER_1] can deliver title as clause 13 requires; (c) the Premises are in the condition clause 12 requires; (d) [SELLER_1] delivers the closing items in Rider clause R8; and (e) the contingencies in Rider clauses R1 to R4 have been satisfied or have properly lapsed. [SELLER_1] is not required to close unless [BUYER_1] pays the price and delivers the documents [BUYER_1] must sign. A party may waive a condition that is for that party's benefit, but only in writing.
- **17. Deed Transfer and Recording Taxes.** [SELLER_1] will pay the New York State real estate transfer tax and will sign and file the transfer tax and real property transfer forms. [BUYER_1] will pay the cost of recording the deed, the mortgage recording tax and the fee for recording the mortgage, and [BUYER_1]'s own title search and title insurance charges. If any other transfer tax applies by law, the party the law makes responsible will pay it. This clause survives closing.
- **18. Apportionments and Other Adjustments; Water Meter and Installment Assessments.** At closing, these are adjusted as of midnight before the closing date, so that [SELLER_1] bears them up to that time and [BUYER_1] bears them afterward: (a) real estate taxes, by the tax period for which each tax is levied, including school tax, town tax and county tax; (b) fuel oil in the tank, which [BUYER_1] will pay [SELLER_1] for at the supplier's current price per gallon, measured by a reading taken shortly before closing, and (c) any other charge that normally is adjusted in a sale like this one. [SELLER_1] reports the annual tax bill at about $11,800, for information only and not as a promise of what future taxes will be. The Premises have a private well and septic system, so no public water meter reading or sewer charge is adjusted. If an installment assessment for a public improvement exists, [SELLER_1] will pay the installments due before the closing date and [BUYER_1] will pay the later ones. If a mistake is found after closing, the parties will correct it promptly by payment between them. This clause survives closing.
- **19. Allowance for Unpaid Taxes, etc..** If, at closing, any tax, water or sewer charge, or similar charge that is a lien on the Premises is unpaid, [SELLER_1] will either pay it before closing or allow [BUYER_1] a credit for the amount due, with any interest and penalty. The title company or closing agent may then pay the charge from the balance due to [SELLER_1].
- **20. Use of Purchase Price to Remove Encumbrances.** [SELLER_1] may use the money due at closing to pay and discharge mortgages, liens and other encumbrances that are not Permitted Exceptions. The title company or closing agent handling closing must pay them directly and deliver recordable satisfactions, or other evidence the title insurer accepts, at closing or afterward as the title insurer agrees to insure over them.
- **21. Title Examination; Seller's Inability to Convey; Limitations of Liability.** [BUYER_1] will order a title search promptly and give [SELLER_1] a written statement of any title objection as soon as [BUYER_1] learns of it. [SELLER_1] will use reasonable efforts to remove any objection that is not a Permitted Exception, but is not required to bring a lawsuit or to spend more than the amount needed to pay mortgages, tax liens and other liens made by [SELLER_1]. If [SELLER_1] cannot or will not cure an objection by the closing date, [BUYER_1] may (a) take the title [SELLER_1] can give, with no reduction in the price, or (b) cancel by written notice, in which case the deposit is returned in full and [SELLER_1] will reimburse [BUYER_1] for the reasonable cost of the title search and any survey, and neither party has any further liability to the other. - **22. Affidavit as to Judgments, Bankruptcies, etc..** [SELLER_1] will give [BUYER_1] and the title company an affidavit stating that no judgment, bankruptcy, tax lien or similar matter affects [SELLER_1] and could become a lien on the Premises. If the title search shows such a matter against a person with a name like [SELLER_1]'s, [SELLER_1] will give the evidence the title company needs to show it is not [SELLER_1]'s.
- **23. Defaults and Remedies.** If [BUYER_1] defaults and does not close when required, and the default is not a result of [SELLER_1]'s failure to perform or of a right of [BUYER_1] to cancel under this contract, [SELLER_1]'s only remedy is to keep the $62,900 deposit as liquidated damages. If [SELLER_1] defaults and does not close when required, and the default is not a result of [BUYER_1]'s failure to perform, [BUYER_1] may either (a) cancel and get back the deposit, with reimbursement of the reasonable cost of the title search, survey, and inspections, or (b) seek a court order requiring [SELLER_1] to sell the Premises as this contract says. A party who wants to claim the other is in default must first give written notice of the default and a reasonable chance to cure it.
- **24. Purchaser's Lien.** [BUYER_1] has a lien on the Premises for the amount of the deposit and any other amounts [SELLER_1] owes [BUYER_1] if this contract ends because of [SELLER_1]'s default or because [BUYER_1] properly cancels. The lien does not apply if [BUYER_1] is in default.
- **25. Notices.** Every notice under this contract must be in writing and must be delivered by hand, by a recognized overnight courier, or by email with a delivery or read confirmation, to the address or email the party writes next to that party's signature. A copy goes to any lawyer the party names there. The notice is effective when delivered, or on the next business day if delivered after 5 p.m. or on a weekend or holiday. The escrow holder and the broker are also given copies of any notice about the deposit or a contingency. Each party may change its address by notice to the others.
- **26. No Assignment.** [BUYER_1] may not transfer or assign this contract, in whole or in part, to anyone else without [SELLER_1]'s prior written consent. Any attempted assignment without that consent is void. [BUYER_1] remains responsible under this contract even if [SELLER_1] consents.
- **27. Broker.** Each party states that the only broker involved in this sale is Hudson Valley AI Realty (a demonstration name), which has acted for both parties as dual agent with each party's written consent, as noted in Rider clause R10. Each party will protect the other against claims for commission or fees by any other broker with whom that party dealt. The broker's commission, if any, is owed only under the separate written agreement with the broker and is payable by the party who agreed to pay it. This clause survives closing.
- **28. Miscellaneous.** This contract, with its Rider and any signed amendment, is the whole agreement of the parties and replaces earlier offers and talks. It binds the parties only when both [SELLER_1] and [BUYER_1] have signed it and a signed copy has been delivered to each. Electronic signatures are valid for this contract and have the same effect as ink signatures, and the parties may sign separate counterparts. Any change must be in writing and signed by both parties. If the Rider conflicts with the body, the Rider controls. The contract binds the parties' heirs and permitted successors. New York law governs. Delivery of the deed ends the parties' duties under the contract, except those that this contract says survive closing. The contract date is the date the last party signs and the signed contract is delivered to the other party. If a deadline falls on a Saturday, Sunday or legal holiday, it moves to the next business day. This draft was prepared as a demonstration and is not a promise that it fits either party's needs; each party may have a lawyer of their choice review it before signing.
- **R1. Mortgage Commitment Contingency.** [BUYER_1]'s obligation to buy depends on [BUYER_1] getting a written commitment from an institutional lender for a conventional mortgage loan on the Premises, in the principal amount shown in [BUYER_1]'s attached pre-approval, within 30 days after the contract date (the Commitment Date). The loan amount, and any other loan terms, are those in the attached pre-approval and are to be confirmed by the parties in writing before signing. [BUYER_1] will apply promptly and in good faith, give the lender what it asks for, and promptly send [SELLER_1] a copy of the commitment or any denial. [BUYER_1] is not required to accept a commitment on terms materially worse than the pre-approval. If by the Commitment Date [BUYER_1] has not received a commitment, [BUYER_1] may cancel this contract by written notice to [SELLER_1] and the escrow holder given on or before the Commitment Date, and the deposit will be returned in full. If [BUYER_1] gives a commitment to [SELLER_1] by that date, or gives no notice of cancellation by that date, this contingency ends, and [BUYER_1] must close even if the lender later refuses to fund, unless the parties extend the date in writing. The parties may extend the Commitment Date only by a written, signed agreement.
- **R2. Home Inspection Contingency.** [BUYER_1]'s obligation to buy depends on a satisfactory home inspection by an inspector of [BUYER_1]'s choice, done within 10 days after the contract date. The inspection covers the whole house and includes the roof, the heating system and the oil tank (including a test of its condition and whether it leaks). [SELLER_1] will allow [BUYER_1] and the inspector reasonable access to the Premises, including the basement, attic, mechanical systems and tank, at times arranged in advance. [BUYER_1] will pay for the inspection and will repair any physical damage the inspection causes. If [BUYER_1] is not satisfied, [BUYER_1] may cancel by written notice to [SELLER_1] and the escrow holder given on or before the 10th day after the contract date, with a copy of the report page or pages that show the problem, and the deposit will be returned in full. Within the same period [BUYER_1] may instead ask [SELLER_1] for repairs or a credit; [SELLER_1] need not agree, and any agreement must be in writing and signed by both parties. A request does not extend the 10 days. If [BUYER_1] gives no cancellation notice by the end of the 10th day, this contingency ends.
- **R3. Well Water Quality and Flow Test.** [BUYER_1]'s obligation to buy depends on a well water quality and flow test showing results [BUYER_1] finds acceptable. The test will be done by a qualified laboratory or well tester of [BUYER_1]'s choice and completed within 10 days after the contract date, the same period as in Rider clause R2. [SELLER_1] will give access to the well and the water supply for sampling and flow testing at times arranged in advance. [BUYER_1] will pay for the test. If [BUYER_1] is not satisfied with the results, [BUYER_1] may cancel by written notice to [SELLER_1] and the escrow holder given on or before the 10th day after the contract date, with a copy of the results, and the deposit will be returned in full. If no notice is given by the end of that day, this contingency ends. The parties may extend this date in writing if the laboratory cannot report in time.
- **R4. Septic Inspection.** [BUYER_1]'s obligation to buy depends on a septic system inspection by an inspector of [BUYER_1]'s choice, done within 10 days after the contract date, the same period as in Rider clause R2. [SELLER_1] will give access to the septic tank, distribution box and drain field, including uncovering the tank cover if it is not already exposed, at times arranged in advance; the cost of any pumping or digging for the inspection is paid by [BUYER_1]. If [BUYER_1] is not satisfied, [BUYER_1] may cancel by written notice to [SELLER_1] and the escrow holder given on or before the 10th day after the contract date, with a copy of the report, and the deposit will be returned in full. If no notice is given by the end of that day, this contingency ends. The parties may extend this date in writing.
- **R5. Personal Property Included.** The accepted offer lists no items of personal property as included in the sale. Nothing other than the fixtures and attached items in clause 1 is included. If the parties want to include an item (for example an appliance or a piece of equipment), they must list it in a written amendment signed by both parties, and [SELLER_1] will then leave it at closing in working order as it is on the contract date and free of liens. Any item not listed belongs to [SELLER_1] and must be removed before closing.
- **R6. Property Condition Disclosure Statement Delivered.** [SELLER_1] will complete and deliver to [BUYER_1] the Property Condition Disclosure Statement on the current New York form (the 2025-07-01 form) before [BUYER_1] signs this contract. At the time this draft was prepared, the statement was still waiting for [SELLER_1] to complete. [BUYER_1] should not be asked to sign until [BUYER_1] has received and had time to read it. Both parties confirm by signing that the statement has been delivered. It is [SELLER_1]'s statement and does not replace the inspections in Rider clauses R2 to R4.
- **R7. Disclosures Not Required for This Sale.** On the facts given, the following are not required and have not been delivered: (a) the lead-based paint disclosure and pamphlet, because the house was built in 1995 and the requirement applies only to homes built before 1978; (b) the agricultural district notice under Agriculture and Markets Law §310, because no agricultural district appears on the record; and (c) the notices under Real Property Law §242, because [SELLER_1] answered no to all four intake questions. - **R8. Closing Items.** At closing, [SELLER_1] will deliver: (a) a signed affidavit that the Premises have working smoke detectors and carbon monoxide detectors as New York law requires; (b) the deed described in clause 14, signed in ink by [SELLER_1] and acknowledged before a notary public; (c) the transfer tax forms and the affidavit in clause 22; (d) keys, garage openers and any codes for the Premises; and (e) the documents the title company reasonably asks for. - **R9. Escrow Holder.** The escrow holder for the $62,900 deposit is to be named by the parties in writing before the deposit is delivered. It must be a third party who is neither [SELLER_1] nor [BUYER_1], and by Hudson Valley custom is often the seller's attorney's escrow account. The escrow holder's name and account details are to be written into this contract before signing, and the escrow holder will sign to accept the duties in clause 6. The contract does not bind the parties until both have signed, even if the deposit has not yet been delivered, but [BUYER_1] will deliver the deposit when both have signed.

Each party understands that the broker may not advise one against the other, and that each party may have a lawyer of their choice review this contract before signing.
- **R11. Property Facts.** Facts about the Premises taken from the public record or from [SELLER_1] and used in preparing this draft are for the parties' information only. They are not promises by [SELLER_1] unless [SELLER_1] also states them in the Property Condition Disclosure Statement. They are: raised ranch built in 1995, 2,520 square feet, 3 bedrooms, 3 full baths, oil heat, private well, private septic, 4.18 acres, Pawling Central School District, FEMA flood zone X (minimal flood hazard), and an annual tax bill of about $11,800. [BUYER_1] should confirm what matters to [BUYER_1], for example during the inspections in Rider clauses R2 to R4.
- **R12. Counting Days.** The contingency periods in this Rider (30 days for the mortgage commitment and 10 days for the home inspection, well water test and septic inspection) count from the contract date, which is the date the last party signs and delivers the signed contract. The closing date, December 22, 2026, is fixed. If the contract date is such that a period ends on a weekend or legal holiday, clause 28 moves it to the next business day.

Side by side:

- 1. Premises: 1, R11: Same substance; adds well, septic and oil tank to the fixtures and lists public-record facts in the Rider.
- 2. Personal Property: 2, R5: No personal property is included; an item may be added only by signed amendment.
- 3. Purchase Price: 3: Same substance; uses $629,000 price, $62,900 deposit (10%) and $566,100 balance.
- 4. Existing Mortgage: 4: Same substance; buyer takes over no mortgage and seller must pay off existing liens.
- 5. Purchase Money Mortgage: 5: Not applicable; no seller financing, only a third-party lender.
- 6. Downpayment in Escrow: 6, R9: Escrow holder is a third party to be named by the parties, with release rules.
- 7. Acceptable Funds: 7: Same substance; wire or bank check at closing, no personal check.
- 8. Mortgage Commitment Contingency: 8, R1: 30-day commitment deadline for a conventional loan; buyer must cancel by that date or the contingency ends.
- 9. Permitted Exceptions: 9: Same substance; permitted exceptions are written for a one-family house.
- 10. Governmental Violations and Orders: 10: Seller cures or credits violations on record before the contract date; buyer may cancel if no agreement.
- 11. Seller's Representations: 11, R6: Seller's statements are to the best of knowledge and are tied to the Property Condition Disclosure Statement.
- 12. Condition of Property: 12, R2, R3, R4: Buyer takes the house as is, subject to a 10-day inspection, well and septic contingencies; seller keeps risk of loss.
- 13. Insurable Title: 13: Same substance; title must be insurable at regular rates.
- 14. Closing, Deed and Title: 14, R8: Deed is signed in ink and acknowledged before a notary.
- 15. Closing Date and Place: 15, R12: Closing is fixed for December 22, 2026; place to be agreed.
- 16. Conditions to Closing: 16, R8: Closing conditions include the contingencies and the smoke and carbon monoxide detector affidavit.
- 17. Deed Transfer and Recording Taxes: 17: Seller pays state transfer tax; buyer pays recording and mortgage recording costs.
- 18. Apportionments and Other Adjustments; Water Meter and Installment Assessments: 18: Adds fuel oil adjustment; no water meter or sewer adjustment because of well and septic.
- 19. Allowance for Unpaid Taxes, etc.: 19: Same substance.
- 20. Use of Purchase Price to Remove Encumbrances: 20: Same substance.
- 21. Title Examination; Seller's Inability to Convey; Limitations of Liability: 21: Seller's duty to cure is limited to money liens; buyer's remedy is deposit back plus search costs.
- 22. Affidavit as to Judgments, Bankruptcies, etc.: 22, R8: Same substance.
- 23. Defaults and Remedies: 23: Seller keeps the 10% deposit as the sole remedy if buyer defaults; buyer may seek a court order or take the deposit back if seller defaults.
- 24. Purchaser's Lien: 24: Same substance.
- 25. Notices: 25: Notices by hand, courier or email, to the addresses the parties write by their signatures.
- 26. No Assignment: 26: Same substance; buyer needs seller's written consent to assign.
- 27. Broker: 27, R10: Hudson Valley AI Realty acts as dual agent with both parties' written consent.
- 28. Miscellaneous: 28, R12: Binds only when both sign; electronic signatures valid; no attorney-approval contingency.

Notes to the parties: This is a demonstration draft. New York law says only a lawyer may draft a contract of sale for another, and each of you may have a lawyer of your choice review this draft before signing. / Fill in or confirm before signing: the escrow holder's name and account, the mortgage loan amount from the pre-approval, the closing place, and each party's address and email for notices. / The seller's Property Condition Disclosure Statement (2025-07-01 form) is still waiting. The buyer should receive and read it before signing. / The deadlines run from the date both of you sign: 30 days for the mortgage commitment and 10 days for the home inspection, well water test and septic inspection; closing is set for December 22, 2026. ## claude-opus-5-5

**Residential Contract of Sale: One-Family House at 146 Route 292, Holmes, NY (Town of Pawling, Dutchess County) (Demonstration Draft)**

- **1. Premises.** [SELLER_1] agrees to sell and [BUYER_1] agrees to buy the land known as 146 Route 292, Holmes, New York, in the Town of Pawling, Dutchess County. The public record shows the lot as about 4.18 acres, improved by a one-family raised ranch house built in 1995. The sale includes all buildings and improvements on the land. It also includes all of [SELLER_1]'s rights in any adjoining streets and roads to their center lines, any easements and rights of way serving the land, and any award for a taking by eminent domain or for damage to the property after the date of this contract. The exact legal description will be the one in [SELLER_1]'s current deed, subject to the title report and any survey.
- **2. Personal Property.** The sale includes the fixtures and articles attached to or used with the house, to the extent they exist on the date of this contract and are owned by [SELLER_1]. These include the heating system and its oil tank, the well pump and water system, the septic system, plumbing, electrical and lighting fixtures, built-in appliances and cabinets, window treatment hardware, and storm windows, doors and screens. These items pass free of liens and with no added payment. No other personal property is included, as Rider R5 confirms. Personal property not listed in R5 is not part of the sale, and [SELLER_1] will remove it before closing.
- **3. Purchase Price.** The purchase price is $629,000, payable as follows: (a) $62,900 (10% of the price) as the downpayment, paid when [BUYER_1] signs this contract and held in escrow under paragraph 6; and (b) $566,100, the balance, paid at closing in funds acceptable under paragraph 7. [BUYER_1] expects to pay part of the balance with the proceeds of the conventional mortgage loan described in paragraph 8 and Rider R1.
- **4. Existing Mortgage.** [BUYER_1] is not taking the property subject to, or assuming, any existing mortgage. [SELLER_1] will pay off and have discharged at or before closing every mortgage and other lien on the property. [SELLER_1] may use part of the balance paid at closing to do so, as paragraph 20 allows.
- **5. Purchase Money Mortgage.** [SELLER_1] is not providing any financing. No part of the price will be paid by a note or mortgage given to [SELLER_1].
- **6. Downpayment in Escrow.** The $62,900 downpayment will be held in escrow by a third-party escrow holder named in writing by both parties before [BUYER_1] signs. By local custom this is usually the seller's attorney's escrow account. The escrow holder (the 'Escrowee') will keep the downpayment in a segregated escrow or attorney IOLA account at a bank in New York State. The Escrowee will not mix it with the Escrowee's own money. Any interest goes to the party who receives the downpayment, unless it is an IOLA account, where by law no interest is paid to either party. The Escrowee will pay the downpayment to [SELLER_1] at closing. If the contract ends before closing, the Escrowee will pay it as the parties jointly direct in writing or as this contract plainly requires. If one party demands the downpayment, the Escrowee will give the other party written notice. If that party objects in writing within 10 business days, the Escrowee will keep holding the money until the parties give joint written instructions or a court with jurisdiction orders its release. The Escrowee may also deposit the money with the clerk of the court. The Escrowee acts only as a stakeholder. The Escrowee is not liable except for willful misconduct or gross negligence, and the parties will share the Escrowee's reasonable costs of any dispute, with the losing party paying them in the end. The Escrowee will sign this contract only to confirm receipt of the downpayment and agreement to these terms. If the Escrowee is the seller's attorney, that attorney may still represent [SELLER_1] in any dispute.
- **7. Acceptable Funds.** All money payable at closing must be paid by wire transfer of immediately available funds to an account named by the payee, or by an official bank check or certified check. The check must be drawn on or issued by a bank or trust company with a New York office, payable to the order of the payee or as the payee directs. A personal check of [BUYER_1] of up to $1,000 may be used for adjustments made at closing. [SELLER_1] may require that funds for paying off liens be in separate checks or wires payable to the lienholders. Each party should confirm wiring instructions by telephone with a known contact before sending money, because wire-fraud emails are common.
- **8. Mortgage Commitment Contingency.** [BUYER_1]'s duty to buy depends on [BUYER_1] getting a written commitment for a conventional first mortgage loan within 30 days after the Effective Date (defined in paragraph 28). The full terms, deadline and cancellation rights are in Rider R1, which controls this subject.
- **9. Permitted Exceptions.** [SELLER_1] will convey the property subject only to the following: (a) zoning, building and land-use laws, as long as the present house and its use as a one-family home do not violate them; (b) recorded covenants, restrictions, easements and agreements, as long as the present house does not violate them and they do not stop use of the property as a one-family home; (c) visible utility lines and poles on, along or under the property that serve it or the area; (d) any facts an accurate survey or inspection would show, as long as they do not make title unmarketable; and (e) unpaid real estate taxes that are not yet due and payable, which will be apportioned under paragraph 18. Anything else that affects title must be removed by [SELLER_1] under paragraphs 13 and 21.
- **10. Governmental Violations and Orders.** [SELLER_1] will comply at [SELLER_1]'s cost with every notice of violation of law or municipal order affecting the property that is noted or issued by the Town of Pawling, Dutchess County, or any other government office on or before the closing date. [SELLER_1] will close it out of record before closing. [SELLER_1] authorizes [BUYER_1] and [BUYER_1]'s title company to search the records of the government offices that have jurisdiction for violations, permits, certificates of occupancy or completion, and open permits. If the house or any addition, deck, garage or finished space lacks a required certificate of occupancy or completion, or has an open building permit, [SELLER_1] will get the certificate or close the permit before closing. If the cost of complying with violations and this paragraph is more than $2,500, [SELLER_1] may choose not to do the work. In that case [BUYER_1] may either accept the property with a credit of $2,500 against the price or cancel this contract and get the downpayment back under paragraph 21.
- **11. Seller's Representations.** [SELLER_1] states, as of the date of signing and again at closing, that: (a) [SELLER_1] is the sole owner of the property and has full power to sell it, and no one else's signature or consent is needed; (b) to [SELLER_1]'s knowledge, no one else has any right to buy, lease or occupy the property; (c) [SELLER_1] is not a 'foreign person' under federal tax law (FIRPTA) and will sign a certificate saying so at closing; (d) [SELLER_1] has received no written notice of any pending or threatened taking by eminent domain, special assessment, or violation not disclosed in writing to [BUYER_1]; (e) to [SELLER_1]'s knowledge, the property is served by a private well and a private septic system that are fully on the property; (f) the property has an oil-fired heating system with an oil tank, and [SELLER_1] will state in the Property Condition Disclosure Statement whether the tank is above ground or buried and what is known about any leak or spill; and (g) the annual property tax bill is about $11,800, as [SELLER_1] has reported. These statements survive closing for one year. A claim on them must be made in writing within that year.
- **12. Condition of Property.** [BUYER_1] has inspected or will inspect the property under Rider R2 to R4 and will accept it in its present condition, subject to normal wear and tear between now and closing and to [BUYER_1]'s rights under the rider. Except for the statements in this contract, the rider and the Property Condition Disclosure Statement, neither [SELLER_1] nor the broker has made any promise about the property's physical condition, its value, the well, the septic system, its taxes or its permitted use. [SELLER_1] will keep the property, including the lawn and grounds, in its present condition until closing. [SELLER_1] will keep insurance on the house until closing, maintain heat to prevent frozen pipes in the winter months, and keep the heating, plumbing, electrical, well and septic systems in working order. [BUYER_1] may inspect the property once within 48 hours before closing, on reasonable notice to [SELLER_1].
- **13. Insurable Title.** [SELLER_1] will give, and [BUYER_1] will accept, title that a reputable title insurance company licensed in New York will insure at its standard rates. That title must be subject only to the permitted exceptions in paragraph 9.
- **14. Closing, Deed and Title.** 'Closing' means the settlement of both parties' duties under this contract: payment of the balance of the price, and delivery to [BUYER_1] of a bargain and sale deed with covenant against grantor's acts, in proper form for recording. The deed will convey fee simple title free of all liens and encumbrances except the permitted exceptions. It will include the covenant required by New York Lien Law §13. It will be signed in ink by every owner and acknowledged before a notary public, as Rider R7 confirms. At closing [SELLER_1] will also deliver the keys, garage door openers, codes, and any manuals and warranties in [SELLER_1]'s possession for the house's systems. [SELLER_1] will give possession vacant and broom-clean, free of all tenants, occupants and personal property not included in the sale.
- **15. Closing Date and Place.** Closing will take place on or about December 22, 2026, which is about 60 days after the contract is signed. It will be held in Dutchess County at the office of [BUYER_1]'s lender or its attorney, or at another place or by remote or escrow closing as the parties agree in writing. Either party may adjourn the closing for a reasonable time by written notice, without making time of the essence. Time becomes of the essence only if one party sends the other a written notice setting a closing date at least 30 days later and stating that time is of the essence for that date.
- **16. Conditions to Closing.** This contract and both parties' duties depend on these conditions: (a) each party has fully performed its duties under this contract and the rider; (b) [SELLER_1]'s statements in paragraph 11 are true and correct at closing; (c) [SELLER_1] delivers the closing items in Rider R7, including the smoke and carbon-monoxide detector affidavit; (d) the house's heating, plumbing, electrical, well and septic systems and all included appliances are in working order at closing; and (e) [BUYER_1]'s mortgage commitment under Rider R1 has been issued and not withdrawn for a reason other than [BUYER_1]'s own fault, unless [BUYER_1] has waived the contingency.
- **17. Deed Transfer and Recording Taxes.** [SELLER_1] will pay the New York State real estate transfer tax on the deed. [SELLER_1] will also sign and deliver the combined transfer tax return (Form TP-584) and pay any costs of recording discharges of [SELLER_1]'s mortgages. [BUYER_1] will pay the fees to record the deed and the filing fee for the real property transfer report (Form RP-5217), which both parties will sign. [BUYER_1] will also pay the mortgage recording tax, title insurance premiums and all costs of [BUYER_1]'s loan. The mansion tax does not apply because the price is below $1,000,000.
- **18. Apportionments and Other Adjustments; Water Meter and Installment Assessments.** The following will be divided between the parties as of midnight of the day before closing: (a) real estate taxes (town, county and school), on the basis of the fiscal period each tax covers; and (b) any other charges customarily apportioned. Fuel oil in the tank will be paid for by [BUYER_1] at closing, at the price per gallon then charged by [SELLER_1]'s supplier. The quantity will be as measured by the supplier within 5 days before closing, and the cost of the reading will be shared equally. The property has a private well and a private septic system, so no water or sewer meter charges are expected. If any such charges or rents apply, they will be apportioned on the last available reading or bill. If an assessment is payable in installments, [SELLER_1] will pay the installments due before closing and [BUYER_1] will take the property subject to the later installments. If the closing tax bill is not yet available, taxes will be apportioned on the last bill and adjusted when the new bill comes out. This adjustment duty survives closing.
- **19. Allowance for Unpaid Taxes, etc..** [SELLER_1] may choose to pay at closing any unpaid taxes, assessments, water charges or similar charges that are liens on the property. [SELLER_1] will do so by allowing [BUYER_1] a credit against the balance equal to the amount due with interest and penalties to the date of closing, as long as official bills are produced. [BUYER_1] will then pay them.
- **20. Use of Purchase Price to Remove Encumbrances.** If at closing there are liens or encumbrances that [SELLER_1] must pay or remove, [SELLER_1] may use part of the balance to do so. [SELLER_1] may do this by paying them at closing or by delivering instruments in recordable form, with recording fees, that the title company accepts. The title company must agree to omit them from [BUYER_1]'s title and loan policies. [BUYER_1]'s lender must also accept this.
- **21. Title Examination; Seller's Inability to Convey; Limitations of Liability.** [BUYER_1] will order a title search promptly after the Effective Date. [BUYER_1] will send [SELLER_1] a copy of the title report and any survey reading as soon as received. [SELLER_1] will act in good faith to clear any title defect that [SELLER_1] must remove under this contract. [SELLER_1] need not start a lawsuit, or spend more than $2,500, to clear defects other than mortgages, judgments and other liens of a fixed amount, which [SELLER_1] must pay. [SELLER_1] may adjourn the closing for up to 60 days to clear a defect. If [SELLER_1] cannot give the title required by this contract, [BUYER_1] has two choices. [BUYER_1] may take whatever title [SELLER_1] can give, with no price reduction except a credit for liens of a fixed amount. Or [BUYER_1] may cancel this contract. If [BUYER_1] cancels, [SELLER_1]'s only liability is to have the downpayment returned and to pay [BUYER_1]'s actual reasonable charges for the title search and any survey. After that neither party has any further duty, except under paragraph 27. This limit does not protect [SELLER_1] from a willful default or a refusal to convey.
- **22. Affidavit as to Judgments, Bankruptcies, etc..** If the title search shows judgments, bankruptcies, liens or similar matters against persons with names the same as or similar to [SELLER_1]'s, [SELLER_1] will deliver at closing an affidavit showing that they are not against [SELLER_1]. The affidavit must be in a form the title company accepts.
- **23. Defaults and Remedies.** If [BUYER_1] wilfully defaults and does not cure after 10 days' written notice, [SELLER_1]'s sole remedy is to keep the $62,900 downpayment as agreed damages. The parties agree that [SELLER_1]'s actual damages would be hard to calculate and that this amount is reasonable. If [SELLER_1] wilfully defaults, [BUYER_1] may choose between two remedies. [BUYER_1] may sue to force the sale (specific performance). Or [BUYER_1] may cancel and get back the downpayment, plus [BUYER_1]'s actual reasonable costs of the title search, survey, inspections and tests. Nothing in this paragraph limits either party's rights under the contingencies in the rider. A party who cancels properly under a contingency is not in default.
- **24. Purchaser's Lien.** Until closing, the downpayment and [BUYER_1]'s reasonable costs of title examination and survey are a lien on the property. This lien does not apply if [BUYER_1] defaults. It does not continue after the contract is properly cancelled and the downpayment refunded.
- **25. Notices.** Every notice under this contract must be in writing. It may be delivered by hand, by a nationally recognized overnight courier, or by email with a copy sent the same day by one of the other methods. It must be sent to the party at the address or email the party gives in writing, with a copy to that party's attorney if one has been named in writing. A party's attorney may give notice for that party. A notice counts as given on the day it is delivered by hand or emailed before 5:00 p.m. New York time on a business day, or the next business day after it is sent by overnight courier. Notices cancelling the contract under the rider must also go to the Escrowee.
- **26. No Assignment.** [BUYER_1] may not assign this contract without [SELLER_1]'s prior written consent. Any attempt to do so without consent has no effect. This contract binds and benefits the parties and their heirs, personal representatives and permitted successors.
- **27. Broker.** Each party states that it has dealt with no real estate broker about this sale other than Hudson Valley AI Realty (a demonstration name). That broker acted for both parties as a dual agent with their written informed consent. [SELLER_1] will pay the broker's commission only if and when closing occurs, under the separate written listing agreement. The commission is not set by this contract. Each party will protect the other from claims by any other broker that party dealt with. This paragraph survives closing or cancellation.
- **28. Miscellaneous.** (a) This contract, with its rider, is the parties' entire agreement and replaces the accepted offer and all earlier discussions. (b) It may be changed or ended only in a writing signed by both parties. (c) This contract is not binding, and is not an offer that can be accepted by conduct, until both [SELLER_1] and [BUYER_1] have signed it, the fully signed contract has been delivered to both, and the Escrowee has received the downpayment. The 'Effective Date' is the date the last party signs and delivers it. All deadlines in the rider run from the Effective Date. (d) Electronic signatures, and signed copies sent electronically, are valid and binding for this contract under New York's Electronic Signatures and Records Act. Counterparts together are one document. The deed and other recordable closing documents must still be signed in ink as Rider R7 provides. (e) 'Days' means calendar days. A deadline falling on a Saturday, Sunday or legal holiday moves to the next business day, ending at 5:00 p.m. New York time. (f) New York law governs. (g) Risk of loss stays with [SELLER_1] until closing under General Obligations Law §5-1311. (h) If the rider conflicts with this body, the rider controls. (i) Only the terms stated to survive will continue after closing; all others merge into the deed.
- **R1. Mortgage Commitment Contingency.** (a) [BUYER_1] will apply in good faith within 5 business days after the Effective Date for a conventional first mortgage loan. The loan will be in the principal amount of $________ (to be filled in by the parties before signing, and not more than the balance of $566,100). It will be for a term of up to 30 years at the lender's prevailing rate and points. [BUYER_1]'s lender pre-approval is attached to this contract. [BUYER_1] will pursue the application diligently, give the lender accurate information, and pay all fees and order the appraisal. [BUYER_1] will keep [SELLER_1] informed on request. (b) The deadline for a written mortgage commitment is 30 days after the Effective Date (the 'Commitment Date'). A commitment counts if it is subject only to conditions within [BUYER_1]'s reasonable control, or to delivery of good title and the usual closing conditions. (c) If [BUYER_1] has not received a commitment by the Commitment Date, or the lender denies the application, [BUYER_1] may cancel this contract by written notice to [SELLER_1] and the Escrowee given on or before the Commitment Date. With the notice [BUYER_1] must send a copy of any denial. The downpayment will then be returned to [BUYER_1] and neither party will have further duties, except under paragraph 27 of the body. (d) If [BUYER_1] does not give that notice by the Commitment Date, this contingency is waived. (e) If a commitment is issued and later withdrawn before closing for a reason not caused by [BUYER_1]'s fault, [BUYER_1] may cancel on the same terms. (f) [BUYER_1] will deliver a copy of any commitment to [SELLER_1] promptly. (g) This contract does not depend on the sale of any other property, and the commitment may not be conditioned on such a sale.
- **R2. Home Inspection Contingency (Including Roof, Heating System and Oil Tank).** (a) Within 10 days after the Effective Date (the 'Inspection Deadline'), [BUYER_1] may have the house inspected at [BUYER_1]'s cost by New York-licensed home inspectors and qualified specialists. The inspection may cover the structure, roof, heating system, electrical and plumbing systems, radon, wood-destroying insects, and the oil tank. If the tank is buried or its location is uncertain, the inspection may include tank location and integrity testing or soil testing near the tank. [SELLER_1] will give reasonable access, with utilities on. (b) If [BUYER_1] is not satisfied with the results, [BUYER_1] may cancel this contract by written notice to [SELLER_1] and the Escrowee given by the Inspection Deadline. The notice must attach the relevant report pages. The downpayment will then be returned. Instead of cancelling, [BUYER_1] may send a written repair or credit request by the Inspection Deadline. If the parties do not sign a written agreement on it within 5 days after the request, [BUYER_1] may cancel by written notice within 2 days after that period. If [BUYER_1] does not cancel, [BUYER_1] accepts the property's condition. (c) If [BUYER_1] gives no notice by the Inspection Deadline, this contingency is waived. (d) [BUYER_1] will repair any damage caused by the inspections. [BUYER_1] will also hold [SELLER_1] harmless from injury or damage claims arising from them. (e) If any inspection finds a leak or spill from the oil tank, [SELLER_1] must report it as New York law requires, whether or not [BUYER_1] cancels.
- **R3. Well Water Quality and Flow Test.** (a) By the Inspection Deadline in R2, which is 10 days after the Effective Date, [BUYER_1] may have the private well tested at [BUYER_1]'s cost. The test must be done by a laboratory certified by the New York State Department of Health's Environmental Laboratory Approval Program (ELAP). It may cover bacteria (total coliform and E. coli), nitrates and nitrites, lead, arsenic and other common contaminants. It may also include a flow (yield) test of the well. (b) The water fails if any result is above the New York State or federal drinking-water standards, or if the flow is below 5 gallons per minute sustained over the test period. (c) If the water or flow fails, [BUYER_1] may cancel by written notice to [SELLER_1] and the Escrowee given within 3 days after receiving the lab report, but not later than 15 days after the Effective Date. The downpayment will then be returned. Instead, [SELLER_1] may offer in writing within that time to install treatment and re-test before closing at [SELLER_1]'s cost. If [BUYER_1] accepts the offer in writing, [BUYER_1] may not cancel for that result. (d) If no notice is given in time, this contingency is waived.
- **R4. Septic Inspection.** (a) By the Inspection Deadline in R2, [BUYER_1] may have the private septic system inspected at [BUYER_1]'s cost by a qualified septic contractor. The inspection may include locating and opening the tank, pumping it, and a hydraulic load or dye test of the system and its absorption field. [SELLER_1] will tell [BUYER_1] what [SELLER_1] knows about the system's location, age and pumping history. (b) If the inspection shows the system is failing, backing up, discharging to the surface, or needs repair or replacement, [BUYER_1] may cancel. [BUYER_1] must give written notice to [SELLER_1] and the Escrowee within 3 days after receiving the report, but not later than 15 days after the Effective Date. The downpayment will then be returned. The parties may instead agree in writing on repairs or a credit. (c) If no notice is given in time, this contingency is waived. (d) [BUYER_1] will pay to restore the grounds after any digging, and to pump the tank if needed for the test.
- **R5. Personal Property Included.** Beyond the fixtures described in paragraph 2 of the body, no personal property is included in the sale. The accepted offer lists none. If the parties want any appliance, furniture, equipment or other movable item to pass with the house, they must list it here in writing before signing. Such items pass at no extra price, in 'as is' condition, free of liens.
- **R6. Disclosures Delivered.** (a) Property Condition Disclosure Statement: New York Real Property Law §462 requires [SELLER_1] to complete the current Property Condition Disclosure Statement (the form revised effective 2025-07-01). [SELLER_1] must give it to [BUYER_1] before [BUYER_1] signs this contract. That form includes the flood-risk questions. At the time of this draft it is still waiting for [SELLER_1] (status CP-04). [BUYER_1] should not sign until [BUYER_1] has received the signed statement. [BUYER_1] will acknowledge receipt in writing, and a copy will be attached to this contract. If [SELLER_1] learns before closing that an answer has become materially untrue, [SELLER_1] will give [BUYER_1] a revised statement. (b) Lead-based paint disclosure and pamphlet: not required, because the house was built in 1995 and the federal rule covers only housing built before 1978. (c) Agricultural district notice (Agriculture and Markets Law §310): not required, because the record shows no agricultural district for the property. (d) Real Property Law §242 seller notices: not required, because [SELLER_1] answered 'no' to all four questions on the intake screen. (e) For information only: public records show FEMA flood zone X, an area of minimal flood hazard and not a special flood hazard area. [BUYER_1]'s lender will make its own flood determination. The public records also show the property is in the Pawling Central School District. Neither statement is a promise by [SELLER_1] or the broker. (f) The dual-agency consent signed by both parties with Hudson Valley AI Realty is on file with the broker.
- **R7. Closing Items.** At closing [SELLER_1] will deliver: (a) the deed described in paragraph 14, signed in ink by every owner and acknowledged before a notary public; (b) an affidavit, as New York Executive Law §378 requires, that working smoke alarms and carbon-monoxide detectors are installed in the house as the law requires; (c) a FIRPTA non-foreign certificate; (d) the signed transfer tax return (Form TP-584) and the real property transfer report (Form RP-5217); (e) payoff letters and discharges, or title-company arrangements for them, for every mortgage and lien; (f) any affidavit required under paragraph 22, and the usual title-company affidavits; (g) the fuel-oil reading under paragraph 18; and (h) keys, openers and codes. [BUYER_1] will deliver the balance of the price and adjustments in funds that meet paragraph 7. [BUYER_1] will also sign the transfer forms and the loan documents.
- **R8. Rider Controls.** This rider is part of the contract. If it conflicts with the body, the rider controls. Each contingency deadline is counted from the Effective Date defined in paragraph 28. Each deadline ends at 5:00 p.m. New York time, moving to the next business day if it falls on a weekend or legal holiday.

Side by side:
